Simulate natural convection in a 2D square cavity using the de Vahl Davis configuration.
The cavity is 1 m by 1 m, with a single cell in the out-of-plane direction to enforce 2D behaviour.
The working fluid is air at 1 atm, with properties evaluated at the mean temperature of 295 K.
The solver is buoyantBoussinesqPimpleFoam.
The Boussinesq approximation is used for the buoyancy source term in the momentum equation.
Gravity is (0 -9.81 0), acting in the negative y direction.
The left wall uses fixedValue T = 300 K.
The right wall uses fixedValue T = 290 K.
The top wall uses zeroGradient T.
The bottom wall uses zeroGradient T.
All four walls use noSlip for velocity.
The initial condition is U = (0 0 0) and T = 295 K throughout the domain.
The Rayleigh number is not imposed; it is determined by the physical parameters (g, beta, deltaT, L, nu, alpha) and the resulting value is reported at the end of the run.
If the resulting Rayleigh number falls outside the range 1e3 to 1e7, flag this to the user before continuing.
Run the simulation to steady state, using a sufficiently small time step to maintain a low Courant number.
Report the final Rayleigh number, the centreline temperature profile, and the centreline velocity profile for comparison against the de Vahl Davis benchmark data.
